title: At Home Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation in Parkinson’s Disease
summary:
This study investigates how non-invasive brain stimulation affects the brains of people with Parkinson's disease and whether such treatment can also be carried out at home.
We use a form of neurostimulation called transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS). This involves applying weak, alternating electrical currents to the scalp via small electrodes — you will feel a slight tingling sensation at most, and no surgery is required. The electrodes are only applied to the scalp temporarily and are removed after each session.
The aim of the study is to examine whether the use of tACS over several days in a home environment is practicable — in other words, whether patients and their relatives can operate the devices safely and how well the treatment works at home.

In addition, 10 healthy people of similar age and sex take part in two short lab sessions without any stimulation: we record their brain activity (EEG) while they do a finger-tapping task. This helps us interpret the brain rhythms we measure in people with Parkinson's disease.

interventions.name:
Gamma transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS)

Participants receive daily gamma-frequency tACS over the primary motor cortex (M1), administered at home using a portable stimulation device. Stimulation is delivered via surface electrodes applying a weak sinusoidal alternating current. A

Sham tACS

Status: Recruitment and measurements of PD patients completed in July 2026 (n = 10).

Healthy control group (exploratory individual gamma frequency (IGF) characterization, no intervention)
10 healthy volunteers, matched 1:1 for age and sex to the PD patients of the pilot cohort. Two laboratory sessions on two consecutive days (approx. 120 min in total) at the University of Oldenburg

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Normal or corrected normal vision, Diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson's disease according to MDS criteria, study companion (caregiver) who can assist the participant with home stimulation.

Healthy controls: normal or corrected-to-normal vision; no diagnosis of Parkinson's disease; no relevant neurological or psychiatric disease; able to perform the aFTT; able to give written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Previous neurological or psychiatric conditions (except Parkinson's disease), use of centrally acting medications (except Parkinson's medication), non-removable metallic objects in/on the body, implanted neurostimulators, epilepsy in personal medical history or immediate family, dementia, MoCA < 21 points, Pregnancy

Healthy controls: relevant neurological or psychiatric disease; diagnosis of Parkinson's disease.
